ImageDescription.value:
Adularia, Chlorite
Locality: Rhône Glacier, Furka, Furka pass area, Goms, Wallis (Valais), Switzerland (Locality at mindat.org)
Size: 10.0 x 8.8 x 6.3 cm.
A classic, older cabinet specimen from the Rhone Glacier of Switzerland. This aesthetic, two-sided specimen features a stacked cluster of sharp, twinned orthoclase variety adularia crystals coated with chlorite on a plate of adularia. The large twin is 6.1 cm across. Nearly pristine. Uncommonly fine quality from this noted locale. Ex. Robert Sullivan Collection and comes with his faded label.

ObjectName.value: Chlorite 001

Categories.value: Self-published work|Crystal structures of chlorites

ImageDescription.value: This image depicts the structure of a chlorite crystal viewed along [001], that is, looking down on the layering. Blue spheres are magnesium or iron; white are oxygen; yellow are hydroxide; black spheres (mostly obscured) are aluminium or silicon.

ObjectName.value: Chlorite 100

Categories.value: Crystal structures|Chlorite|Self-published work

ImageDescription.value: This image shows the crystal structure of chlorite viewed along [100], that is, looking along the layers of the crystal. Blue spheres are magnesium or iron; small black spheres (mostly hidden) are silicon or aluminium; white spheres are oxygen; yellow spheres are hydroxide. A TOT (talc) layer is visible at the center of the image, with O (brucite) layers bonding it to the next TOT layers at the top and bottom of the image.

Categories.value: Flickr images reviewed by FlickreviewR 2|Files from James St. John Flickr stream|Chlorite schist

ImageDescription.value:
Chlorite schist (greenschist) from California, USA.

Chlorite schist is a moderately common, intermediate- to high-grade, foliated metamorphic rock. It is principally composed of chlorite, a group of silicate minerals with a greenish-gray color. This example is from California's Pelona Schist. The precursors were deep-water marine, fine-grained, siliclastic sedimentary rocks. The rock also has some albite feldspar.

Stratigraphy: Pelona Schist, undetermined age (possibly Cretaceous or Paleocene)

Locality: lower plate rocks beneath the Vincent Thrust Fault, San Antonio Canyon, southern flanks of the San Gabiel Mountains, San Bernardino County, southern California, USA
